desc:
Given an unsorted integer array nums, an integer k and an integer target, find the k elements of nums that are closest to target, where the distance of x is |x - target|.

If two elements are equally close, the smaller value is considered closer. Repeated values are separate elements. Return the chosen k values in ascending order.

For example, nums = [10, 1, 4, 7, 8], k = 3, target = 6 gives [4, 7, 8]. With nums = [1, 5], k = 1, target = 3 both are at distance 2, so the smaller value wins: [1].
hints: Define a distance for each element and think about ordering the elements by it.
Sort by the key (|x - target|, x). The tie rule is built into the second component.
Take the first k elements of that order, then sort them by value for the output.
editorial: Sort the elements by the key (abs(x - target), x). The key is a strict total order on values (equal values are interchangeable), so the first k elements are exactly the k closest, with the smaller-value tie-break applied. Finally sort those k values ascending for the output.

This is O(n log n). With a heap or quickselect on the same key you can reduce it to O(n log k) or O(n) average. If the input were already sorted, binary search for the left edge of the best window of length k would give O(log n + k).
